item.title: Work on proposals to restrict or remove mortgage interest tax relief for Island landlords ongoing
item.description: GOVERNMENT officials are continuing work on proposals that could see mortgage interest tax relief for landlords restricted or removed, the Treasury Minister has confirmed. item.description: A LEGAL loophole that allows medical professionals found unfit to practise in the UK to continue working in Jersey is due to be closed as part of a new law aiming to overhaul the current “piecemeal” system for policing health and social care professionals in Jersey. item.title: Last year was the fourth hottest on record
item.description: LAST year was the fourth hottest year on record, with the Island experiencing an average temperature of 13.3°C. A dark red stripe will be added to the Climate Wall mural at the Waterfront to mark this. item.title: More than muscle: push to encourage more women to join the fire service
item.description: FOR generations, firefighting has been viewed as a male-dominated profession, shaped by physical stereotypes and outdated perceptions. item.title: Jersey’s population now estimated to top 105,000 – but growth slowing
item.description: THERE are now an estimated 105,540 people living in Jersey – an increase of 510 from the previous year, marking the third year in a row that has seen a rise in population. However, the government’s latest population report – released today – also showed that the rate of growth was slowing. item.title: Work on St Catherine’s breakwater to begin next month
item.description: ST Catherine’s breakwater is to undergo ground investigation work next month, as engineers prepare to drill into its ageing structure to help guide future repairs.
